name: Cobra Push-Up
description: The cobra push-up begins in a downward-dog position and dips the body forward in a sweeping arc until the chest is near the floor, then extends the spine into a cobra-like backbend. This movement trains the chest at the bottom of the arc while also opening the thoracic spine, shoulders, and hip flexors through a full-body coordinated motion.

execution.starting_position: Begin in a downward-facing dog position: hips high, arms and legs straight, forming an inverted V with the body.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment needed. Clear enough floor space for a full-body extended position.
steps: Step 1: Start in a downward-dog position with hips elevated.
Step 2: Bend the elbows and dip the head and chest forward and down toward the floor in a sweeping arc.
Step 3: As the chest passes between the hands, begin extending the elbows and driving the hips toward the floor.
Step 4: Fully extend the arms and open the chest upward into a cobra or upward-dog back extension.
Step 5: Reverse the motion or return to the downward-dog position to complete one rep.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you dip forward and down. Inhale as you extend up into the cobra position.
common_mistakes: Skipping the arc and just doing an up-down movement
Letting the hips touch the floor during the dip phase
Not opening the chest fully at the top
safety_considerations: Avoid if you have lumbar spine issues — the cobra extension loads the low back
Warm up wrists and shoulders before performing
Progress from a modified version if thoracic mobility is limited
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: The dip phase brings the chest close to the floor between the hands. The cobra phase extends fully overhead without letting the hips touch down.
coaching_cues: Dive down through the arms, not straight into the floor
Open the chest to the sky at the top
Think about drawing a 'U' shape with your body
